decisions.reason: The current complete report explicitly reanalyses the same ADNI baseline temporal-lobe phenotype/data stream as Stein2010a and compares GRIN2B/NRXN3 association evidence against its published findings, using LASSO SNP selection and joint gene tests. The recovered complete Stein manuscript establishes original baseline provenance, temporal phenotype and named associations. Original N742 and current N729 reflect differing selection/covariates; exact individual intersection is unverified, but no new ADNI wave supplies the retest. Reanalysing the original observations under an alternative gene specification can qualify even when method development and discovering additional genes are the main aims. The independent Brisbane MACROD2 component repeats a new within-paper discovery and does not turn the Stein retest into new-data replication. Joint gene tests are not claimed to recover marginal SNP coefficients. Original NRXN3 is a liberal P<1e-5 association, despite the current summary describing genome-wide significance; that contradiction is preserved. The dependent original binding and separate reproduction axes require necessary updated review; no outcome is inferred solely from stronger p values.

decisions.reason: Under the parent source adjudication establishing reproduction (opening421_boundary_types_0281.parent.json), Kohannim et al. (2012) reanalyze the same ADNI-1 baseline 1.5-T MRI tensor-based morphometry bilateral temporal-lobe volume phenotype and genotype data stream as Stein et al. (2010a) (with N = 729 vs. N = 742 after Mach imputation, MAF > 0.10, intragenic SNP restriction, and MDS covariates) using gene-centric LASSO selection and multi-SNP partial F-tests, and explicitly compare the resulting gene-level associations for GRIN2B, NRXN3, and sub-threshold ADAMTS2 against Stein et al. (2010a). The reference list (offsets 80300–81400) uniquely identifies Stein et al. (2010a), 'Genome-wide analysis reveals novel genes influencing temporal lobe structure with relevance to neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease,' NeuroImage, 51, 542–554 (DOI: 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.02.068), matching the shipped original identity and the recovered full text. The Brisbane twin cohort (N = 564) tests MACROD2, a novel within-paper discovery, while Stein et al. (2010b) and Hibar et al. (2011a) are cited for vGWAS/imputation and principal-component gene methods rather than the univariate temporal-lobe GWAS target claims.

decisions.reason: The original-data analysis goes directly to LASSO-selected joint-gene tests, rather than recovering the original742-person marginal-SNP coefficients/specification; outcome_computation is not checked under CodebookAxis1Rule1. For the retested gene-association evidence, reasonable separate selection/testing specifications materially qualify the in-sample support: fivefold nested selection/test averages reach no gene-wide significance, and ten split-half trials retain only GRIN2Bwithout the claimed boost. The authors identify unstable selected SNPs in small selection sets. This is a robustness challenge to the association evidence under the alternative specifications actually tested, not proof that a specific original SNP coefficient reversed or that the genes have no biological effect. Original NRXN3passed only a liberal threshold, despite current genomewide summary; lower sample sizes and changed gene-versus-SNP targets are explicit qualifications, so no direct original-number recovery or new-population effect is inferred. MACROD2Brisbane results concern the paper's new discovery and are not transferred to Stein. The raw reply used invalid not_applicable/mixed axis words; they remain rejected unchanged. Parent independently applied the actual codebook vocabulary and the full Cross-validation/Discussion/Methods plus Stein original, rather than repairing raw output.

previous_decisions.quote: We tested the reliability and reproducibility of our top genetic association findings in an independent non-overlapping young adult cohort. Our goal was to see if the results could be replicated in a cohort scanned on a different continent, with a different scanner field strength, and with a roughly 50-year difference in mean age.
previous_decisions.reason: This study applies a gene-centric LASSO regression method to discover novel gene associations with temporal lobe volume in ADNI and then tests its own newly discovered top hit (MACROD2) in an independent young adult cohort. Under the codebook, replicating a new finding discovered within the same paper is not a replication of a previously published finding, and earlier GWAS results (Stein et al., 2010a) serve only as a methodological benchmark.
